content.text: Infect of middle ear, temporal bone, & mastoid air cells
Clin defn: bulging TM or new-onset otorrhea ⍉← acute OE - MC reason for abx in children
MC infants & young children - can also develop in adults
, FHx, day care, pacifier or bottle use,
· M. catarrhalis · S. pyogenes - ↓S. pneumoniae ← PCV13 vax
fluid accum behind blocked tube → infected - USU preceded or followed by OME (uninfected middle ear fluid)
Eustachian tube dysfun (ETD) = MC contributing factor
Infants & young children: ear rubbing or tugging · fussiness · restlessness · poor feeding · vomiting · diarrhea
•TM opaque or cloudy · acute perf w otorrhea
•TM may appear pale or yellow w pus behind
•light reflex ↓ or absent (norm TM → bright light reflex)
•norm: aerated middle ear - TM translucent · slightly convex · mobile
Effusion + acute inflam → mod-severe otalgia · fever · bulging erythematous TM - sx develop rapidly over 24-48hrs - may have otorrhea or pus
Clin dx - children: pneumatic otoscopy ⍉always performed → dx w signs of middle ear effusion & inflam (bulging TM)
Tympanocentesis for a sample of fluid for cx - definitive (for recurr cases)
•amoxicillin first line esp if ⍉β-lactam w.in last 30d · ⍉purulent conjunctivitis · ⍉Hx of recurr AOM
: cephalosporin (cefdinir · ceftriaxone) - macrolides (azithro · clarithromycin) ⍉indicated ← pneumococcal resistance - fallback only if PCNs & cephalosporins both precluded
•TMP-SMX: ⍉role in empiric tx ← S. pneumoniae & H. flu resistance - only if documented suscep & preferred agents ⍉usable
•Augmentin first line if β-lactam w.in last 30d · purulent conjunctivitis (otitis-conjunctivitis syndrome) · Hx of recurr AOM ← H. flu (can be amoxicillin-resistant · Augmentin-suscep)
•consider observation period if ≥2yo · immunocompetent & mild sx
•immediate abx vs watchful waiting (start abx if sx worsen or ⍉improve after 48-72hrs) - based on age · parental preference · severity
•immediate abx: <6mo · 6mo-2yo (unilat or bilat) · ≥2yo toxic-appearing · persistent otalgia 48hrs · fever ≥102.2°F in past 48hrs · uncertain f/u
•watchful waiting: 6mo-2yo w mild sx (mild otalgia · fever <102.2°F) & unilat · ≥2yo w mild sx & ⍉otorrhea
•⍉topical benzocaine for ear pain if <2yo - risk of methemoglobinemia - ⍉topical analgesics (benzocaine · lidocaine) if TM perf
Fluid in middle ear w.o s/sxs of acute infect
: develops after viral URI or AOM - inflam & Eustachian tube dysfun (ETD) impair drainage of middle ear secretions
: recent URI · allergic rhinitis · day care · tobacco smoke exposure · craniofacial abnorm (cleft palate) · conditions assoc w ETD
Hearing difficulty · ear fullness · speech & language concerns - USU ⍉pain or fever
•dull or opaque TM w air-fluid level or visible bubbles
Middle ear effusion w.o acute inflam findings
Dull TMs w air-fluid levels & ⍉marked bulging → OME (vs AOM)
•abx · corticosteroids · antihist & decongestants ⍉improve outcomes in uncomp OME
if persistent effusion w sig hearing loss · speech delay · recurr episodes or struct abnorm of TM
Inflam of the external auditory canal
” - rise in pH allows bact overgrowth
(use of Q-tips · scratching) · age 7-12 (can occur at any age) · aberrant ear wax
•occlusive ear devices (earplugs · earphones · hearing aids) · prev radiation · derm conditions (allergic contact derm · psoriasis · atopic derm)
•staph aureus & epidermis · GABHS · proteus · anaerobes · aspergillus · fungi
in the ear canal (may have recent hx of swimming)
Malodorous auricular d/c · ear P or fullness · hearing loss (if severe canal swelling)
pain on traction of the ear canal or tragus
•pain w pinna or auricle mvt - canal erythematous & edematous ± debris (yellow · brown · white · gray)
of external auditory canal w erythema · debris or d/c
TM USU norm unless canal swelling blocks view - norm mobility on pneumatic otoscopy
•otic aminoglycoside or FQ ± topical glucocorticoid → relieves pruritus & pain
•mild (minimal canal edema · minor discomfort & pruritus): acetic acid-hydrocortisone otic drops
•mod (canal partially occluded by edema · intermed pain & pruritus): topical abx + glucocorticoid (cipro-hydrocortisone · neomycin-polymyxin B-hydrocortisone)
•severe (canal completely occluded · intense pain & pruritus): same drops + wick - deep tissue involvement → add systemic cipro or ofloxacin
•otomycosis (fungal OE): clotrimazole otic solution BID x10-14d
•⍉further mech trauma - drying agent (1:1 isopropyl alc & white vinegar) acidifies ear
if sig canal edema - helps topical abx enter
•IS or DM w persistent OE → refer for specialty eval
Invasive infect of external auditory canal & skull base
(temporal bone · soft tissue & cartilage) - comp of acute OE - osteomyelitis of skull base in IS or DM pts - w.o prompt tx may extend into middle fossa floor · clivus · contralat skull base
older pts w DM (↑cerumen pH · ear canal microangiopathy) - children: rare - underlying malig (leukemia) or malnourished
Pseudomonas (found in H2O) - often Hx of aural H2O exposure - less common: S. aureus · Aspergillus fumigatus (fungal) · Proteus mirabilis · Klebsiella oxytoca · Burkholderia cepacia
May extend via fissures of Santorini (vertical fissures in anterior external auditory canal cartilage)
•may radiate to TMJ joint (pain w chewing)
•otorrhea unresponsive to tx · periauricular pain · swelling
•more severe pain · nocturnal pain · pain w chewing vs uncomp OE - ⍉respond to topical tx
•children: fever · leukocytosis · bacteremia - facial n. involvement more likely (closer to ear canal than adults) - CN 9 · 10 · 11 at jugular foramen
•comp: meningitis · brain abscess · dural sinus thrombophlebitis
severe auricular pain on traction of the ear canal or tragus
•exquisite tenderness of external ear · purulent otorrhea · macerated granulation tissue
ddx Bell palsy (HSV): unilat CN 7 palsy - ⍉eyelid closure · facial droop · hyperacusis · pain around jaw - ⍉granulation tissue or otorrhea
: edema of the external auditory canal w erythema · d/c ·
granulation tissue @ the bony cartilaginous junction of the ear canal floor
· frank necrosis of the ear canal skin
Clin + labs + imaging: ↑ESR & CRP (monitor course) · gram stain & cx of granulation tissue or drainage · blood cx
CT → early bone erosion · MRI → extent of dz & monitor tx response
•IV cipro → PO cipro once clin improvement & ↓ESR/CRP
•bony erosion or multi CN neuropathies: cipro + antipseudomonal β-lactam (piperacillin · piperacillin-tazobactam · ceftazidime · cefepime · meropenem)
Infect of the mastoid air cells of the temporal bone
: MC comp of untx AOM - suppurative ext of infect into mastoid air cells
: S. pneumoniae · H. flu · M. catarrhalis · S. aureus · S. pyogenes
Early & sufficient tx of AOM = most important factor to ↓risk
CT w contrast of temporal bone
•if dx unclear → fluid in mastoid air cells · irreg mastoid cortex
IV abx + middle ear or mastoid drainage (myringotomy) +/- tympanostomy tube placement
•uncomp: admit · IV abx + middle ear drainage (myringotomy) - PO abx alone or myringotomy alone insuff
•⍉recent abx & ⍉recurr OM: ampicillin-sulbactam alone - recent abx or recurr OM: piperacillin-tazobactam
•comp (meningitis · epidural or subdural abscess · facial n. palsy · labyrinthitis · hearing loss · osteomyelitis · venous sinus thrombosis) → mastoidectomy + IV abx + myringotomy
MC occur ← penetrating or noise trauma
Comp of AOM: ↑middle ear P → central ischemia → necrosis → perf
Perforated AOM: nontypeable H. flu = MC isolated pathogen (esp infants & toddlers)
Pts w otalgia prior to rupture may develop
sudden pain relief w bloody otorrhea
AOM-related perf: defect of TM on otoscopy w concurrent otorrhea
90% heal in a few mo - TM capable of regen
Topical ofloxacin: children w tympanostomy tubes w otorrhea or traumatic perf (contaminated H2O) - ⍉studied in acute perf ← AOM
Keep ear dry · analgesics · abx for contaminated injuries
AOM w perf: PO amoxicillin or Augmentin x10d - ⍉azithro (spont perf → likely H. flu → Augmentin first line)
: refer to ENT for further eval (surg)
